# GA-readiness assessment for Llama Stack

## Description

Resolve the strategy's central unknown: no systematic GA-readiness assessment
of Llama Stack has been done, and TP feedback is scattered across support
tickets. This investigation inventories the gaps between current Tech Preview
quality and the GA bar — across API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits,
and error handling — and produces the definitive GA scope that downstream
stability and hardening work is planned against.

## Scope

- Systematically collect and triage TP feedback from support tickets.
- Audit the published API surface for stability gaps (unversioned or
  unstable APIs, undocumented behavior).
- Assess upgrade paths from the last two TP releases.
- Identify scale limits of the current distribution (supported sizes,
  concurrency, resource bounds).
- Review error handling across the API layer and distribution.
- Classify each identified gap by severity against the GA bar.
- Produce the assessment report and the definitive GA scope: which gaps are
  in scope for GA, which are deferred, with rationale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gap inventory covers all four assessment axes — API stability, upgrade
  paths, scale limits, error handling — with each gap classified by severity
  and the GA-bar criterion it fails.
- TP feedback from support tickets is systematically collected and mapped to
  inventory entries; no untriaged ticket themes remain.
- The assessment report states the definitive GA scope, including explicit
  in-scope and deferred gap lists with rationale for each deferral.
- The assessment report and GA scope are published and reviewed with the
  owning team and product stakeholders.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between
  current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits,
  error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. This epic is that
  assessment.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantees and GA hardening

## Description

Deliver the published API surface stability guarantee for Llama Stack:
versioned APIs, a deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last
two TP releases — and close the quality gaps that the GA-readiness
assessment places in the definitive GA scope. The size and content of this
work is an estimate until that assessment lands; this epic's scope is written
against the assessment's definitive GA scope and is rewritten if the
assessment's findings differ from the estimate.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning on the published Llama Stack API surface.
- Define and document a deprecation policy for the published API surface.
- Implement and test the upgrade path from each of the last two TP releases
  to the GA release.
- Remediate the quality gaps that the GA-readiness assessment places in the
  definitive GA scope — error handling, scale-limit gaps, and related
  hardening items. Scale-limit gaps the assessment places in the GA scope
  land in this epic, not merely in the support posture's configuration
  matrix.
- Carry all changes through the existing Konflux build pipeline for the
  Llama Stack midstream repository.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned, and the versioning scheme is
  documented.
- A deprecation policy for the published API surface is documented and
  applied to the GA release.
- Upgrade from each of the last two TP releases to the GA release is tested;
  the procedure and results are recorded and repeatable.
- Every quality gap included in the definitive GA scope is remediated, or
  explicitly deferred with recorded rationale.
- All changes pass the existing Konflux build pipeline for the Llama Stack
  midstream repository.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: Published API surface carries a stability guarantee:
  versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last
  two TP releases. This epic delivers that guarantee, plus the hardening work
  the GA scope defines.

# Llama Stack production support posture

## Description

Put the production support posture in place for Llama Stack GA: documented
SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix. This
epic produces the support-facing commitments that distinguish a GA component
from a Tech Preview one. The supported configuration matrix is aligned to the
definitive GA scope produced by the GA-readiness assessment, so this epic is
gated on that assessment landing; support-posture gaps the assessment surfaces
land as scope additions here.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA Llama Stack distribution
  (the operational quality dimensions the support organization commits to).
- Define and document the backport policy: which releases receive fixes,
  for how long, and how fixes are delivered.
- Define and publish the supported configuration matrix: deployment
  configurations and provider combinations supported at GA.
- Align the supported configuration matrix with the definitive GA scope
  produced by the GA-readiness assessment.
- Review the support posture documents with the support organization and
  publish them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets for the GA distribution are documented and published.
- The backport policy is documented and published, covering supported
  releases and fix-delivery mechanics.
- The supported configuration matrix is published and reflects the
  definitive GA scope from the GA-readiness assessment.
- The support posture documents are reviewed with the support organization.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P0)**: Production support posture is in place: documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. This epic
  delivers all three.

# Supported TrustyAI guardrails integration for Llama Stack GA distributions

## Description

Promote TrustyAI safety guardrails from an experimental flag to a supported,
documented integration for Llama Stack GA distributions. After this epic,
a GA distribution can enable TrustyAI guardrails through a supported
configuration path instead of a TP-era experimental opt-in. The
user-facing integration documentation (configuration steps and supported
scenarios) is authored in the Llama Stack GA documentation uplift, not in
this epic; this epic delivers the engineering side of the integration.

## Scope

- Replace the experimental opt-in flag with a supported configuration path
  for TrustyAI guardrails in Llama Stack GA distributions.
- Validate the integration in a reference deployment (Llama Stack
  distribution with TrustyAI guardrails functioning end to end).
- Carry all changes through the existing Konflux build pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- TrustyAI guardrails can be enabled in a Llama Stack GA distribution
  through a supported configuration path, with no experimental flag.
- A reference deployment demonstrates guardrails functioning through the
  integration.
- The replacement is recoverable for rollback: the supported configuration
  path can be disabled, and disabling it restores the previous behavior of
  no TrustyAI guardrails enabled (the experimental opt-in behavior remains
  recoverable during the GA transition).
- All changes pass the existing Konflux build pipeline for the Llama Stack
  midstream repository.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. This epic
  delivers the Llama Stack distribution side of that integration; the
  TrustyAI-side validation is tracked separately by the TrustyAI team, and
  the integration documentation is authored in the Llama Stack GA
  documentation uplift.

Validate and support the TrustyAI side of the guardrails integration with
Llama Stack GA distributions. TrustyAI itself is already GA; this epic
verifies that TrustyAI guardrails work correctly as a supported integration
target of the Llama Stack GA distribution and remediates or files any
TrustyAI-side incompatibilities. The TrustyAI-side integration guidance
(supported versions and configurations) is authored in the Llama Stack GA
documentation uplift from this epic's validation results; this epic records
those results as the input to that documentation.

## Scope

- Define and execute a validation matrix of guardrails scenarios against a
  Llama Stack GA distribution (fairness/bias, drift, and guardrail behavior
  as exposed through the integration).
- Confirm compatibility of the TrustyAIService CRD and metrics API surfaces
  with the Llama Stack GA distribution.
- Remediate TrustyAI-side issues found, or file them with a recorded
  disposition.
- Record the validated supported versions and configurations of the

  integration guidance authored in the GA documentation uplift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation report is produced covering the guardrails scenarios executed
  against a Llama Stack GA distribution, with recorded results.
- TrustyAI-side compatibility is confirmed, or every issue found is
  remediated or filed with a recorded disposition.
- The validation report states the supported versions and configurations of
  the integration confirmed by validation, available as input to the
  GA documentation uplift.

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented

# Enable Llama Stack management in the Dashboard by default for entitled clusters

## Description

Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management in the
Dashboard: on entitled clusters, the Llama Stack management surface is
available by default, with no configuration change required. Clusters
without entitlement keep the current behavior.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard feature-flag default for Llama Stack management from
  opt-in to enabled-by-default, gated on cluster entitlement.
- Verify that non-entitled clusters are unaffected (Llama Stack management
  not surfaced by default).
- Verify the Llama Stack management surface renders and operates correctly
  against an entitled cluster with default configuration.
- Carry the change through the existing Konflux build pipeline for the
  Dashboard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with default Dashboard configuration, the Llama
  Stack management surface is available without any opt-in flag change.
- On a cluster without entitlement, the Dashboard behavior is unchanged:
  Llama Stack management is not surfaced by default.
- The default flip is revertible: reverting the feature-flag default to its
  previous opt-in value restores the Tech Preview opt-in gate behavior, and
  this rollback path is documented.
- The change passes the existing Konflux build pipeline for the Dashboard.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5 (P1)**: The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default
  for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). This epic delivers that default
  enablement.
